hardware: AMD RYZEN AI MAX+ PRO 395 / Radeon 8060S (laptop; gross numbers; provisional pending the desktop gfx1151)
change: Item 3 of docs/UD-OPTIMIZED-ROUTE-PLAN.md. Raw dense IQ4_XS/IQ3_XXS prefill routes to the existing source-shaped integer-MMQ kernel instead of the strict per-row GEMV. The kernel addresses weights as qweight + expert*expert_bytes + out_row*weight_row_bytes, so at expert 0 it consumes the dense raw GGUF layout unchanged: the dense route is the degenerate single-expert case. No repack, no weight sidecar, no new kernel.
scope: gfx1151 only by design. The dense kernel keys are registered on both HIP backends through the normal gfx1151 alias path, but only gfx1151 declares GGUF_IQ_DENSE_MMQ_PREFILL_POLICY, so the route is inert on gfx1100 pending its own qualification. The selected/MoE keys remain gfx1100-only and are asserted so by test.

mechanism.admission: An execution owner binds a bounded workspace (iq_dense_mmq_session); the backend policy then selects quant and row range. Without a bound workspace every raw-IQ projection keeps the strict GEMV owner.
mechanism.constraints: in_features % 256, out_features % 128, bf16 output, rows >= 32. min_rows is a crossover not a capability: the GEMV re-reads the weight column once per 8-row slab, so the MMQ only wins once a prompt spans several slabs.
mechanism.workspace: Q8_1 K-major DS4 activation plane plus a small per-rows metadata tail (expert_start_compact, expert_start_mmq, tile_expert). Metadata is uploaded once per distinct row count, not per projection. Sized for 1024 rows x max(hidden, ffn, ssm_inner); ~10 MB for this model, allocated separately from the F16 staging buffer so the planar-Q6 integer route and this one do not share an owner.
mechanism.decode: rows=1 is below min_rows, so decode is untouched by construction.

numerics.reading: The MMQ arm has the best mean of any default measured (0.0010796 against 0.0012376 and 0.0012709) and recovers the top-1 position the role-coverage step lost. This is agreement with a llama.cpp teacher while adopting llama.cpp's own MMQ dataflow, so part of the improvement is convergence toward the reference implementation rather than evidence of higher absolute quality. It should not be quoted as a quality win without a BF16-teacher or task gate.
